purpose.question: Can a restarting endpoint reject stale or replayed policy epochs and resume only the current safe configuration?
purpose.comparison: Command acceptance before restart, immediately after restart, and after fresh synchronization.
purpose.primary_metric: Number of invalid policy applications after the deliberate restart.

_todo.action: Prove the normal command path and boot identity observability before injecting a restart.
_todo.method: Reuse a valid safety-capable Thread topology, assign an endpoint target, record how its boot ID changes after reset, and verify that one current authenticated finite-TTL policy can be accepted and acknowledged under normal conditions.
_todo.done_when: A pre-restart trace contains active run identity, endpoint boot ID, accepted epoch, TTL, and acknowledgement reason.

_todo.action: Run one controlled restart and explicitly enumerate the replay attempts that follow it.
_todo.method: Choose endpoint_restart time after stable operation, capture duration through reattachment, then send the ordinary gateway path an old epoch, an expired command, and a wrong-run command. Never bypass authentication or call private apply functions directly.
_todo.done_when: The ready file fixes restart time and target, while operator notes list the exact invalid command cases and expected reject reasons.

_todo.action: Make zero invalid policy applications the safety outcome and preserve complete command evidence.
_todo.method: Set safety treatment, select only the bounded bulk-rate action, require the endpoint to fall back until fresh synchronization, preserve critical service floor and counter reconciliation, and require command-audit, raw events, final counters, versions, and run status artifacts.
_todo.done_when: A reviewer can reconstruct every attempted command and confirm that stale, replayed, or wrong-run input changed no endpoint policy.
